sources.title: Attention lecture
sources.content: Self-attention lets each token weigh the importance of every other token in the same sequence. An input embedding is projected into a query (Q), key (K), and value (V). Attention scores are computed as softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ)V. The scale factor prevents dot products from becoming too large. Unlike recurrent networks, self-attention can relate distant tokens directly.

sources.title: Transformer textbook
sources.content: A transformer layer combines multi-head attention with a position-wise feed-forward network, residual connections, and layer normalization. Multiple attention heads learn different relationships in parallel. Positional encodings add information about token order, since attention by itself has no inherent concept of sequence position.

sources.title: Cross-attention lecture
sources.content: Queries are the questions asked by each token and keys are descriptions that help match relevant information. Values hold the information that gets mixed together. Cross-attention uses queries from one sequence and keys and values from another sequence.
